revealWordProblem.title: Apply: Studio Recording Costs
revealWordProblem.text: A music studio charges a flat $50 booking fee plus $35 for each hour of recording time. Let h represent the number of hours a band records. Write an algebraic expression for the total cost the band will pay.
revealWordProblem.sampleAnswer: 35h + 50. The $35 per hour is multiplied by the variable h (the number of hours), and the flat $50 booking fee is the constant that is added once.

vocabulary.definition: A power uses a base and an exponent to show repeated multiplication.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una potencia usa una base y un exponente para mostrar multiplicación repetida.

vocabulary.definition: A small number that tells how many times to multiply a number by itself.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Un número pequeño que dice cuántas veces multiplicar un número por sí mismo.
vocabulary.visual: In 2³, the small 3 means multiply 2 by itself 3 times: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8
vocabulary.cloze: The small raised number that shows how many times the base is multiplied is the ___.

examples.why: The 3 is the base, not the exponent.

vocabulary.definition: Find the value of an expression by substituting numbers and following the order of operations.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Hallar el valor de una expresión sustituyendo números y siguiendo el orden de las operaciones.

vocabulary.definition: A letter that stands for a number that is unknown or can change.
vocabulary.definitionEs: Una letra que representa un número desconocido o que puede cambiar.
vocabulary.visual: In 3x + 5, x can be any number — if x = 2, the expression equals 11; if x = 10, it equals 35
vocabulary.cloze: A letter that stands for an unknown number, like x, is a ___.

launch.narrative: Missed a lesson — or just want a refresher? This catch-up station reviews Lessons 6.1–6.3: 6.1 Powers and Exponents, 6.2 Evaluate Expressions, 6.3 Write Algebraic Expressions. Read the Big Ideas, warm up with the review problem, then prove you're caught up in the mixed practice.

conceptIntro.heading: The Big Ideas — Lessons 6.1–6.3
conceptIntro.intro: Here is the one thing to remember from each lesson, plus a quick guided example. If one of these feels shaky, that lesson is right above this one in the menu — you can open it any time.
conceptIntro.keyIdea: 6.1: A power like 2³ is a short way to write repeated multiplication: 2 × 2 × 2. • 6.2: Replace the variable with its number, then follow the order of operations to find the total. • 6.3: Words like "each" or "per" mean multiply, and "plus" or "more than" mean add.

iDo.title: The Big Ideas (one per lesson)
lines: Lesson 6.1 — Powers and Exponents: A power like 2³ is a short way to write repeated multiplication: 2 × 2 × 2.
Lesson 6.2 — Evaluate Expressions: Replace the variable with its number, then follow the order of operations to find the total.
Lesson 6.3 — Write Algebraic Expressions: Words like "each" or "per" mean multiply, and "plus" or "more than" mean add.

explore.instructions: Read each word phrase and sort it into the correct algebraic expression.

items.text: 5 more than a number n → n + 5
the sum of 12 and a number x → 12 + x
a number y increased by 8 → y + 8
7 less than a number p → p − 7
a number w decreased by 3 → w − 3
the product of 4 and a number m → 4m

discourse.prompt: What key words helped you decide which operation to use? How can the same phrase be written differently?
discourse.sentenceFrame: The phrase '___ ' tells me to use ___ because the key word ___ means ___.

optional.stem: (Lesson 6.1) The drum loop plays 3⁴ beats. What is the value of 3⁴?
optional.explanation: 3⁴ means use 3 as a factor 4 times: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. It is NOT 3 × 4 = 12.
choiceFeedback: Did you multiply the base by the exponent instead? Try: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3.
Check the value. Is 7 anywhere in this power?
That's 3³. Count how many 3's to multiply in 3⁴.
optional.stemEs: El bucle de batería toca 3⁴ tiempos. ¿Cuál es el valor de 3⁴?
optional.explanationEs: 3⁴ significa usar 3 como factor 4 veces: 3 × 3 × 3 × 3 = 81. NO es 3 × 4 = 12.
hints: In a power, the small raised number counts how many times the base is used as a factor — it is not something you multiply by.
Write the power out as repeated multiplication before you compute anything.
3⁴ means 3 × 3 × 3 × 3. Multiply the first two to get 9, then keep multiplying by 3 for each factor that is left.
hintsEs: En una potencia, el número pequeño de arriba cuenta cuántas veces se usa la base como factor; no es algo por lo que se multiplica.
Escribe la potencia como multiplicación repetida antes de calcular nada.
3⁴ significa 3 × 3 × 3 × 3. Multiplica los dos primeros para obtener 9 y sigue multiplicando por 3 con cada factor que queda.

optional.stem: (Lesson 6.2) Track 1 — The beat formula is 3x + 5, where x is the number of bass drops. Evaluate 3x + 5 when x = 4.
optional.explanation: Substitute x = 4: 3(4) + 5. Multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12. Then add: 12 + 5 = 17.
choiceFeedback: Evaluate 3 × 4 = 12 first, then add 5.
Substitute x = 4: 3(4) + 5 = 12 + 5 = 17, not 27.
Did you follow order of operations? Multiply before adding.
optional.stemEs: Pista 1: La fórmula del ritmo es 3x + 5, donde x es la cantidad de golpes de bajo. Evalúa 3x + 5 cuando x = 4.
optional.explanationEs: Sustituye x = 4: 3(4) + 5. Multiplica primero: 3 × 4 = 12. Después suma: 12 + 5 = 17.
hints: Evaluating means replacing the variable with its value and then following the order of operations.
Substitute 4 for x, then handle the multiplication before the addition.
Write 3(4) + 5. Multiply 3 × 4 first, then add the 5 to finish.
hintsEs: Evaluar significa reemplazar la variable por su valor y después seguir el orden de las operaciones.
Sustituye 4 en lugar de x y luego resuelve la multiplicación antes de la suma.
Escribe 3(4) + 5. Multiplica primero 3 × 4 y después suma el 5 para terminar.

optional.stem: (Lesson 6.3) Line 1: A lyric says '7 more than a number of beats n.' Which expression matches?
optional.explanation: 'More than' means addition, so '7 more than n' is n + 7.
choiceFeedback: 'More than' means you add to the number. Start with n and add 7.
'7 more than n' is not 7 times n. It's n increased by 7.
'More than' means add. Start with n, then add 7.
optional.stemEs: Verso 1: una letra dice '7 más que un número de tiempos n'. ¿Qué expresión corresponde?
optional.explanationEs: 'Más que' significa adición, así que '7 más que n' es n + 7.
hints: Find the key word in the phrase — it names the operation you need.
'More than' is an addition signal, and addition can be written in either order.
So you are combining n and 7 with a plus sign. Write that expression out.
hintsEs: Busca la palabra clave de la frase: ella nombra la operación que necesitas.
'Más que' es una señal de suma, y la suma se puede escribir en cualquier orden.
Entonces estás combinando n y 7 con un signo de más. Escribe esa expresión.

choiceFeedback: Did you multiply base by exponent (4 × 3)? The exponent counts how many 4's.
Look at the power: 4³ has a 4 and a 3, but not 43.
That's not matching the repeated multiplication 4 × 4 × 4.
hints: Look at the small raised 3. That exponent counts how many 4's get multiplied — it is not a number to multiply 4 by.
Rewrite the power as repeated multiplication first, then multiply one step at a time.
Write 4³ as 4 × 4 × 4. Multiply the first pair (4 × 4 = 16), then multiply that result by the last 4.
hintsEs: Mira el pequeño 3 elevado. Ese exponente cuenta cuántos 4 se multiplican; no es un número por el que se multiplica el 4.
Reescribe primero la potencia como multiplicación repetida y luego multiplica paso a paso.
Escribe 4³ como 4 × 4 × 4. Multiplica el primer par (4 × 4 = 16) y luego multiplica ese resultado por el último 4.

choiceFeedback: Did you multiply base by exponent? Write 6 × 6 instead.
That mixes the digits. Is the power 62 or 6²?
hints: The little 2 is the exponent. It counts how many 6's you multiply — it's not a number to add or multiply by.
Turn the power into repeated multiplication before you calculate anything.
Rewrite 6² as 6 × 6, then multiply those two factors.
hintsEs: El pequeño 2 es el exponente. Cuenta cuántos 6 multiplicas; no es un número para sumar ni para multiplicar.
Convierte la potencia en multiplicación repetida antes de calcular nada.
Reescribe 6² como 6 × 6 y luego multiplica esos dos factores.

choiceFeedback: 3x means 3 times x. Substitute and multiply first: 3 × 4 = 12, then add 7.
Did you add 3 + 4 + 7 instead of multiplying 3 × 4? Remember: 3x means 3 times x.
12 + 7 = 19. Did you multiply 3 × 4 first?
hints: 3x means 3 times x — there's a hidden multiplication between the 3 and the x.
Substitute 4 in place of x, multiply first, then add 7.
Replace x: the expression becomes 3(4) + 7. Start by multiplying 3 × 4, then add the 7.
hintsEs: 3x significa 3 por x: hay una multiplicación escondida entre el 3 y la x.
Sustituye 4 en lugar de x, multiplica primero y luego suma 7.
Reemplaza x: la expresión se vuelve 3(4) + 7. Empieza multiplicando 3 × 4 y luego suma el 7.

choiceFeedback: 2n means 2 times n. Substitute n = 6: 2 × 6 = 12. Then 20 − 12 = 8.
Did you add instead of subtract? Follow order of operations: multiply 2 × 6 first.
20 − 12 = 8. Did you calculate 2n correctly?
hints: 2n means 2 times n. Substituting means swapping n for 6 everywhere it appears.
Order of operations: do the multiplication 2 × 6 before subtracting from 20.
Rewrite as 20 − 2(6). First find 2 × 6, then subtract that product from 20.
hintsEs: 2n significa 2 por n. Sustituir es cambiar n por 6 en todos los lugares donde aparece.
Orden de las operaciones: haz la multiplicación 2 × 6 antes de restar de 20.
Reescribe como 20 − 2(6). Halla primero 2 × 6 y luego resta ese producto de 20.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 6.3) Which expression represents 'the product of 6 and a number n'?
approaching.explanation: 'Product' means multiplication, so the product of 6 and n is 6n.
choiceFeedback: 'Product' is the result of multiplication. 6 times n is 6n.
Adding 6 + n is not the same as 'the product of 6 and n'.
'Product' = multiply. 'Sum' = add. 6 and n multiplied is 6n.
hints: Underline the key word 'product.' Every operation has a code word — which operation does 'product' name?
Test with plain numbers: the product of 6 and 2 is 12. Which operation turned 6 and 2 into 12?
Use that same operation to join 6 and n. Writing a number right next to a variable shows it.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué expresión representa 'el producto de 6 y un número n'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Producto' significa multiplicación, así que el producto de 6 y n es 6n.
hintsEs: Subraya la palabra clave 'producto'. Cada operación tiene su palabra clave: ¿qué operación nombra 'producto'?
Pruébalo con números simples: el producto de 6 y 2 es 12. ¿Qué operación convirtió 6 y 2 en 12?
Usa esa misma operación para unir 6 y n. Escribir un número justo al lado de una variable ya lo indica.

approaching.stem: (Lesson 6.3) Which expression represents '9 less than a number y'?
approaching.explanation: 'Less than' means subtract from the number, so it's y − 9.
choiceFeedback: The order is flipped here. '9 less than y' starts at y and takes 9 away, so y has to come first in the subtraction.
This adds 9 instead of taking it away. The phrase 'less than' signals subtraction.
'Less than' flips the order: the number comes first, then subtract.
hints: 'Less than' is a tricky phrase — it flips the order of what you write.
Try it with numbers: '9 less than 20' means 20 − 9, not 9 − 20. Start with the amount you're taking from.
Copy the number pattern: '9 less than 20' → 20 − 9. Use the same order with y in place of 20.
approaching.stemEs: ¿Qué expresión representa '9 menos que un número y'?
approaching.explanationEs: 'Menos que' significa restar del número, así que es y − 9.
hintsEs: 'Menos que' es una frase tramposa: invierte el orden de lo que escribes.
Pruébalo con números: '9 menos que 20' significa 20 − 9, no 9 − 20. Empieza con la cantidad de la que quitas.
Copia el patrón numérico: '9 menos que 20' → 20 − 9. Usa el mismo orden con y en lugar de 20.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 6.1) Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: 2⁴ does NOT mean 2 × 4. The exponent 4 tells you to use the base 2 as a factor 4 times: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2 = 16. So 2⁴ = 16, not 8.
hints: Count how many 2's you should multiply: the exponent 4 means four factors of 2.
Write 2⁴ as repeated multiplication first: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2, then multiply step by step.
onLevel.explanation: The "Student's thinking" step turns 2⁴ into 2 × 4. The exponent 4 is a count, not a factor: it says to use the base 2 four times, giving 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. Doubling step by step gives 2, 4, 8, 16, so 2⁴ = 16, not 8.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso "Student's thinking" convierte 2⁴ en 2 × 4. El exponente 4 es una cuenta, no un factor: indica usar la base 2 cuatro veces, o sea 2 × 2 × 2 × 2. Duplicando paso a paso da 2, 4, 8, 16, así que 2⁴ = 16, no 8.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 6.1) Evaluate each exponential expression. Show the repeated multiplication and the final value.
hints: Each row shows the repeated multiplication for you. Your job is to multiply the factors carefully.
Multiply left to right, keeping a running total. For 10⁴, watch the zeros pile up.
Row 1: 4 × 4 = 16, then 16 × 4 gives the value. Use the same running-total idea for the other rows.
onLevel.explanation: Multiply the listed factors with a running total: 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, 2⁶ = 64 as well after six doublings, 5³ = 125, and 10⁴ = 10,000. Notice that 4³ and 2⁶ have the same value even though the bases and exponents differ, and that 10⁴ gains one zero for each factor of 10.
onLevel.explanationEs: Multiplica los factores que aparecen llevando un total acumulado: 4³ = 4 × 4 × 4 = 64, 2⁶ también da 64 después de seis duplicaciones, 5³ = 125 y 10⁴ = 10,000. Fíjate en que 4³ y 2⁶ tienen el mismo valor aunque las bases y los exponentes sean distintos, y en que 10⁴ gana un cero por cada factor de 10.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Evalúa cada expresión exponencial. Muestra la multiplicación repetida y el valor final.
hintsEs: Cada fila te muestra la multiplicación repetida. Tu trabajo es multiplicar los factores con cuidado.
Multiplica de izquierda a derecha llevando un total parcial. En 10⁴, observa cómo se acumulan los ceros.
Fila 1: 4 × 4 = 16 y luego 16 × 4 da el valor. Usa la misma idea del total parcial en las demás filas.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 6.2) Spot the Common Mistake
onLevel.correctWork: 5(6) − 3 = 30 − 3 = 27. Follow the order of operations: multiply 5 × 6 = 30 FIRST, then subtract 3. There are no parentheses around 6 − 3, so you cannot subtract before multiplying.
hints: In 5 × 6 − 3, which operation comes first — the multiplication or the subtraction?
There are no parentheses grouping 6 − 3, so multiply 5 × 6 = 30 first, then subtract 3 to get 27.
onLevel.explanation: The step subtracted before multiplying, which would only be allowed if parentheses grouped 6 − 3. In 5(6) − 3 the multiplication comes first: 30 − 3 = 27. Inventing that grouping turned the problem into 5(6 − 3) and produced 15 instead.
onLevel.explanationEs: En ese paso se restó antes de multiplicar, lo cual solo se permitiría si un paréntesis agrupara 6 − 3. En 5(6) − 3 la multiplicación va primero: 30 − 3 = 27. Inventar ese agrupamiento convirtió el problema en 5(6 − 3) y dio 15 en su lugar.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 6.2) Evaluate each expression for the given value of the variable.
hints: The Substitution column already replaced the variable for you — your job is to finish the arithmetic.
Use order of operations: parentheses first, then exponents, then multiply, then add or subtract.
Row 1: 5(6) − 3. Multiply 5 × 6 first, then subtract 3. Row 2 needs the exponent 3² before adding.
onLevel.explanation: The substitutions are already written, so the work is the order of operations. 5(6) − 3 multiplies first: 30 − 3 = 27. 3² + 4 handles the exponent first: 9 + 4 = 13. 2(5 + 8) clears the parentheses first: 2(13) = 26. And 40 − 3(7) multiplies before subtracting: 40 − 21 = 19.
onLevel.explanationEs: Las sustituciones ya están escritas, así que el trabajo es el orden de las operaciones. 5(6) − 3 multiplica primero: 30 − 3 = 27. 3² + 4 resuelve primero el exponente: 9 + 4 = 13. 2(5 + 8) resuelve primero el paréntesis: 2(13) = 26. Y 40 − 3(7) multiplica antes de restar: 40 − 21 = 19.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Evalúa cada expresión para el valor dado de la variable.
hintsEs: La columna de Sustitución ya reemplazó la variable por ti: tu trabajo es terminar la aritmética.
Usa el orden de las operaciones: primero paréntesis, luego exponentes, luego multiplicar y luego sumar o restar.
Fila 1: 5(6) − 3. Multiplica 5 × 6 primero y luego resta 3. La fila 2 necesita el exponente 3² antes de sumar.

onLevel.title: (Lesson 6.3) Spot the Common Mistake

workedExample.label: Reasoning
workedExample.work: I saw 'divided by' so I wrote the variable first and then 8.

onLevel.correctWork: '8 divided by a number m' means start with 8 and divide it by m: 8 ÷ m. Division is not commutative, so order matters — m ÷ 8 means something different (a number m divided by 8).
hints: What number comes first in '8 divided by m'?
Test it: 8 divided by 2 is 4, but 2 divided by 8 is 0.25 — order changes the answer.
onLevel.explanation: The expression step wrote the variable first, but "8 divided by a number m" starts with the 8 and splits it. Division is not commutative, so the correct translation is 8 ÷ m — with m = 2, 8 ÷ 2 = 4 while 2 ÷ 8 = 0.25.
onLevel.explanationEs: El paso de la expresión escribió primero la variable, pero "8 dividido entre un número m" empieza con el 8 y lo reparte. La división no es conmutativa, así que la traducción correcta es 8 ÷ m: con m = 2, 8 ÷ 2 = 4 mientras que 2 ÷ 8 = 0.25.

onLevel.instructions: (Lesson 6.3) Match each word phrase to its correct algebraic expression.

items.text: a number b divided by 5 → b ÷ 5
the sum of a number d and 15 → d + 15
10 decreased by a number r → 10 − r
4 more than triple a number c → 3c + 4
half of a number h → h ÷ 2

hints: Each card already pairs a phrase with an expression. Check that the expression truly matches the phrase.
Translate the phrase yourself first, then compare your expression with the card's before placing it.
First card: 'twice a number k' means two of them. Does 2k say that? If yes, it's correctly matched.
onLevel.explanation: Checking a card means translating the phrase yourself and comparing: twice k is 2k, b divided by 5 is b ÷ 5, the sum of d and 15 is d + 15, 10 decreased by r is 10 − r, 4 more than triple c is 3c + 4, and half of h is h ÷ 2. All six pairings hold up, so every card belongs in Correctly Matched.
onLevel.explanationEs: Revisar una tarjeta significa traducir la frase por tu cuenta y comparar: el doble de k es 2k, b dividido entre 5 es b ÷ 5, la suma de d y 15 es d + 15, 10 disminuido en r es 10 − r, 4 más que el triple de c es 3c + 4, y la mitad de h es h ÷ 2. Las seis parejas se sostienen, así que todas las tarjetas van en Emparejado correctamente.
onLevel.instructionsEs: Une cada frase con su expresión algebraica correcta.
hintsEs: Cada tarjeta ya empareja una frase con una expresión. Revisa que la expresión de verdad coincida con la frase.
Traduce tú mismo la frase primero y luego compara tu expresión con la de la tarjeta antes de colocarla.
Primera tarjeta: 'el doble de un número k' significa dos de ellos. ¿Dice eso 2k? Si sí, está bien emparejada.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.1) Find the Exponent Error
extending.correctWork: 2³ means 2 × 2 × 2, NOT 2 × 3. The exponent tells us to multiply the base by itself 3 times: 2 × 2 × 2 = 8.
hints: Does the exponent mean to multiply the base BY the exponent, or to multiply the base BY ITSELF that many times?
Write out what 2³ means as repeated multiplication: 2 × ___ × ___.
extending.explanation: The "Student's thinking" step reads 2³ as 2 × 3, which is multiplication by the exponent rather than repeated multiplication of the base. Written correctly, 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2, so 2 × 2 = 4 and 4 × 2 = 8. The value is 8, not 6.
extending.explanationEs: El paso "Student's thinking" lee 2³ como 2 × 3, lo que es multiplicar por el exponente en lugar de multiplicar la base repetidamente. Escrito correctamente, 2³ = 2 × 2 × 2, así que 2 × 2 = 4 y 4 × 2 = 8. El valor es 8, no 6.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.2) Find the Evaluation Error
extending.correctWork: 4(2²) + 3 = 4(4) + 3 = 16 + 3 = 19. Square the 2 first, THEN multiply by 4.
hints: Order of operations: what should happen first — squaring the 2, or multiplying 4 × 2?
The exponent applies only to x, not to 4x. Evaluate 2² = 4 first, then multiply by 4.
extending.explanation: The exponent in 4x² belongs only to x, not to 4x, so the work cannot be rewritten as (4 × 2)². Square first: 2² = 4, then multiply by 4 to get 16, then add 3 for 19. Treating it as 8² inflated the answer all the way to 67.
extending.explanationEs: El exponente en 4x² pertenece solo a x, no a 4x, así que el trabajo no se puede reescribir como (4 × 2)². Primero se eleva al cuadrado: 2² = 4, luego se multiplica por 4 para obtener 16 y después se suma 3 para llegar a 19. Tratarlo como 8² infló la respuesta hasta 67.

extending.title: (Lesson 6.3) Find the Translation Error

workedExample.label: Reasoning
workedExample.work: I see 'less than' so I subtract, and 12 comes first in the phrase.

extending.correctWork: '12 less than a number g' means start with g and subtract 12: g − 12. The phrase 'less than' reverses the order — the number being subtracted FROM comes after 'less than.'
hints: Does '12 less than g' mean start with 12 or start with g?
Try it with numbers: '5 less than 20' means 20 − 5 = 15, not 5 − 20.
extending.explanation: The expression step copied the numbers in the order they appear, but "less than" reverses them. "12 less than a number g" starts at g and takes 12 away, so it is g − 12 — the same way "5 less than 20" means 20 − 5 = 15.
extending.explanationEs: El paso de la expresión copió los números en el orden en que aparecen, pero "menos que" los invierte. "12 menos que un número g" empieza en g y le quita 12, así que es g − 12, igual que "5 menos que 20" significa 20 − 5 = 15.

optionalActivity.name: Catch-Up Challenge
optionalActivity.intro: Mix it up: pick the right lesson's big idea for each problem — that's the real catch-up skill.

practice.commonMistake: A common mistake in Write Algebraic Expressions is treating 'each' or 'per' as if it means add instead of multiply, and attaching the variable to the wrong number. For 'a $25 setup fee plus $8 per hour, h,' students often write 25 + 8 + h (adding all three numbers) or 25h + 8 (multiplying the flat fee by h) instead of the correct 8h + 25. Since $8 applies per hour, it must multiply the variable (8h), and the flat $25 fee is a constant added only once — check that the per-unit rate, not the flat fee, is the number multiplied by the variable.

diagram.title: Studio Cost: 25 + 8h
diagram.caption: Each bar is the total cost 25 + 8h; the $25 base (0 hr) stays fixed and every extra hour adds $8.

connect.scenario: A music studio charges a $25 setup fee plus $8 per hour of recording time. Let h represent the number of hours.
connect.promptQuestion: Write an expression for the total cost. What does each part of the expression represent?
connect.prompt: The total cost is ___ + ___h. The ___ represents the ___ and ___h represents the ___.

check.stem: Which expression models the total cost for h hours?
check.explanation: The $25 setup fee is charged once (a constant) and $8 is charged for every hour (8h).

check.stem: What is the total cost for 6 hours?

check.explanation: The coefficient is the number multiplied by the variable — here 8, the hourly rate. 25 is the constant.

connect.modelAnswer: The total cost is 25 + 8h. The 25 is the constant: a one-time $25 setup fee that never changes. The 8 is the coefficient of h — $8 for each hour of recording. For 6 hours that is 25 + 8(6) = $73.

exitTicket.stem: (Catch-up check, from Lesson 6.2) Evaluate 5(n − 3) + 2 when n = 7.
exitTicket.explanation: Do the parentheses first: 7 − 3 = 4. Then multiply: 5 × 4 = 20. Then add: 20 + 2 = 22. (If you got 34, you multiplied 5 × 7 first and ignored the parentheses instead of subtracting 3 before multiplying. If you got 20, you found 5(7 − 3) correctly but forgot to add the 2 at the end. If you got 18, you subtracted 2 instead of adding it.)
choiceFeedback: 5 × 7 = 35 is not right here — do parentheses first: 7 − 3 = 4, then 5 × 4 = 20, then add 2.
The parentheses come first: 7 − 3 = 4. Then multiply and add.
Order of operations: parentheses (7 − 3 = 4), multiply (5 × 4 = 20), then add (20 + 2 = 22).
hints: Notice the parentheses around n − 3. Order of operations says handle inside them before multiplying.
Substitute 7 for n, do the subtraction inside the parentheses, multiply by 5, and add 2 last.
Write 5(7 − 3) + 2. First step: 7 − 3 = 4, so it becomes 5(4) + 2. Multiply next.

questions.stem: Which expression means '5 less than twice a number n'?
questions.explanation: Twice n is 2n. Five less than that is 2n − 5.

steps.prompt: Write the base as repeated factors: ___.

parallelPractice.stem: (Lesson 6.3) Write an expression for 4 more than 2 times a number x.
hints: Re-read the question. What exactly is it asking you to find?
Use the visual model, then complete one step at a time.
Start like this: “2 times x” becomes 2x.
parallelPractice.explanation: “2 times x” becomes 2x. “4 more” means add 4. Write the full expression: 2x + 4.

hintsEs: Vuelve a leer la pregunta. ¿Qué te pide encontrar exactamente?

Empieza así: “2 veces x” se convierte en 2x.
parallelPractice.explanationEs: “2 veces x” se convierte en 2x. “4 más” significa sumar 4. Escribe la expresión completa: 2x + 4.
